clue.text: Draws the 17 across who is booked as a 15

definitions.meaning: draws are lotteries in which tickets win prizes

definitions.text: the 17 across who is booked as a 15
definitions.meaning: the safe-breaker of E. W. Hornung's stories, written up as an amateur cricketer and society figure

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a burglar who appears in books as a gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references point at CRACKSMAN (17 across) and GENTLEMAN (15 across): A. J. Raffles is the gentleman thief of Hornung's novels.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotteries for prizes share the name of Hornung's fictional cracksman, the amateur gentleman burglar.

clue.text: Under friction image becomes a boundary for Caesar

indicators.note: in a down entry the image sits below the friction

parts.note: rub, the act of friction
an icon is an image

explanation.surface: Rubbing a picture turns it into a frontier for a Roman general.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rubicon was the river Julius Caesar crossed in 49 BC, the border of his province.
explanation.definitionFit: The river crossed by Julius Caesar marked the limit of his province: a frontier.

clue.text: Fabricate a lure of beer at fourpence a quart

indicators.note: to make up or construct, so the letters are built into a new order

explanation.surface: Concoct a bait of beer sold cheaply by the quart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fabricate' acts on A LURE OF to give the old name for cheap ale.
explanation.definitionFit: An old cheap ale was named for its price of four pence per quart.

clue.text: Room for scientific work on the Spanish trade mark

parts.note: lab, short for laboratory
el is Spanish for 'the'

explanation.surface: A laboratory set up on a Spanish brand name.
explanation.definitionFit: A brand name used by a company, such as a record company, is a label.

clue.text: Precious stone located beneath geological layers by artifice

indicators.note: in a down entry the stone comes below the layers

parts.note: strata are layers of rock
a gem

explanation.surface: A jewel is found under layers of rock by trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse or trick is a piece of artifice, cunning scheming.

clue.text: Gets away as English sun goes to the head-up to a point

indicators.note: the first letters go in front of the next piece in the run
the head runs right up to the compass point, which follows it

parts.note: S is an abbreviation for sun, as in Sunday
a head is a headland, which is another word for a cape
S is a compass point, south

explanation.surface: Heading up to a sunny English promontory, someone gets away from it all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Head' means a headland here, not the top of the body, and 'a point' is a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: To make an escape is to get free or flee; the verb form matches 'gets away'.

clue.text: Two directions to institute legal proceedings succeed

parts.note: E and N, east and north
to sue is to take legal action

explanation.surface: Two instructions for starting a lawsuit both win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' means follow on, not win.
explanation.definitionFit: To come after or follow is the old sense of succeed, a synonym.

clue.text: She sings the lowest songs!

parts.note: the lowest female singing voice belongs to this singer, not a singer of the poorest songs

explanation.surface: A singer whose songs are the worst of all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lowest' seems to mean worst, but it means deepest in pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: The deepest-pitched female voice belongs to this kind of singer.

clue.text: Crazy to check turnover in East Germany

indicators.note: the run of both pieces is turned over and read backwards

parts.note: mad
stop, halt

explanation.surface: Madness holding back a revolution in the old East Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turnover' reverses MADSTOP as a whole. Potsdam lay in the former German Democratic Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: The city near Berlin was in the former German Democratic Republic.

clue.text: Operator who gives needless counsel to the waves

definitions.meaning: one who performs operations in a hospital

definitions.text: who gives needless counsel to the waves
definitions.meaning: one telling the sea to keep surging, which it does anyway

explanation.surface: A man gives pointless advice to the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as SURGE ON, the word is advice the waves do not need.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor who performs operations; split as two words, it is an instruction to keep surging.

clue.text: Sob from the cetacean

definitions.meaning: to weep noisily
the fat taken from a whale

explanation.surface: A weeping fit set off by a whale.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: to weep noisily, and the thick fat stripped from whales.

clue.text: American politician involved in treason

indicators.note: the letters of the word are tangled up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A US lawmaker caught up in a plot against the state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' reads as being caught up in something; 'involved' is the anagram signal working on TREASON.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the US Senate is a typical American politician.

clue.text: Apple woman who provided a match for a Georgian sovereign

definitions.meaning: an apple dessert baked in a bread-lined mould

definitions.text: woman who provided a match for a Georgian sovereign
definitions.meaning: the queen who married King George III

explanation.surface: A woman selling apples found a wife for one of the Georges.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Charlotte of Mecklenburg-Strelitz married George III; 'apple' is the baked pudding, an apple charlotte.
explanation.definitionFit: The pudding and George III's queen share one name, a dessert and a royal consort.

clue.text: High pressure region created by discordant dirge

indicators.note: out of harmony, so the word's letters are set into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A mournful song played out of tune produces a weather front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discordant' suits a song in the surface, but it signals an anagram of DIRGE.
explanation.definitionFit: In meteorology an elongated area of high atmospheric pressure is called by this name.

clue.text: Nice setting for oriental kinswoman

indicators.note: the city is the setting that holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: the French city's name, taken as a word
E for East, the oriental direction

explanation.surface: The Riviera city is the backdrop for a relative from the East.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice the French Riviera city, read as the word NICE, has E put inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a female relative, a kinswoman.

clue.text: Is he husky because of the cold?

definitions.text: Is he husky because of the cold?

parts.words: Is he husky because of the cold?
parts.note: a husky voice can come from a cold; here husky is the Arctic sled breed

explanation.surface: Is his voice hoarse because he has a cold?
explanation.walkthrough: 'husky' suggests a hoarse voice; it is the sled dog of the Arctic.
explanation.definitionFit: The husky is an Arctic sled breed, bred for cold.

clue.text: As a non-professional cricketer he's a courteous fellow

definitions.meaning: an amateur player, as in the old Gentlemen v Players match
a polite, well-mannered man

explanation.surface: An amateur cricket player is also well mannered.
explanation.walkthrough: Until 1962 English first-class cricket split amateurs (Gentlemen) from paid professionals (Players).
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket's old term for an amateur was also the word for a polite, well-bred man.

clue.text: Half-way through course at the club?

definitions.text: Half-way through course at the club?

parts.words: Half-way through course at the club?
parts.note: a golf course has eighteen holes, so half of them marks the turn

explanation.surface: Midway through a meal at one's club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a meal and 'club' a social club; it is a golf course and golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard golf round is eighteen holes, so half a round is this number.

clue.text: Mr C. can ask to be reclassified as house-breaker

indicators.note: put into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man named Mr C. asks to be moved into a different category.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of MRCCANASK, signalled by 'to be reclassified', gives the old word for a safe-breaker.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a burglar or safe-breaker who cracks open safes and houses.

clue.text: Have a talk with a bad actor on the Medway

parts.note: chat
a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: Talking with a poor performer by the river.
explanation.walkthrough: Chatham is a dockyard town on the River Medway in Kent, south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kent naval dockyard town stands on the River Medway.

clue.text: Ban it as ordered; refrain from using

indicators.note: put in order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Prohibit it as instructed and do without.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as ordered' signals an anagram of BAN IT AS.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstain is to hold back from indulging, as from drink.

clue.text: Sequence of command

definitions.meaning: arrangement in a series
an instruction to be obeyed

explanation.surface: A run of instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: arrangement one after another, and an instruction given by authority.

clue.text: Stubborn member of the Middlesex Regiment's 1st Battalion

definitions.meaning: an obstinate person who will not give in
a soldier of the regiment nicknamed for its stand at Albuera

explanation.surface: An obstinate soldier of a famous English regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The Middlesex Regiment, formerly the 57th Foot, earned the nickname at Albuera in 1811.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstinate holdout; also the nickname of the Middlesex Regiment's soldiers.

clue.text: Sounds gently like the cattle thief does

definitions.meaning: makes a soft crackling noise
steals livestock

explanation.surface: A soft noise, as a cattle thief makes at work.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: makes a soft dry whisper, and steals livestock.

clue.text: Neddie found before morning on the Burmese border

indicators.note: the animal is placed in front of the morning

parts.note: a neddy or neddie is a donkey, an ass
AM, ante meridiem, for morning

explanation.surface: A donkey is spotted at dawn at the frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: The Indian state of Assam borders Myanmar (Burma).
explanation.definitionFit: This north-eastern Indian state shares a frontier with Myanmar, then called Burma.

clue.text: Ideal situation for one prepared to work like a horse

definitions.text: Ideal situation for one prepared to work like a horse

parts.words: Ideal situation for one prepared to work like a horse
parts.note: a horse at work is strapped into its tack; a person still working is said to be in the same state

explanation.surface: The perfect setup for someone ready to toil like a carthorse.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means still at work, from a horse strapped into its tackle for pulling.

clue.text: Industry minus effort equals a flower of the East

indicators.note: with the attempt taken away from the word

parts.note: a try is an attempt, an effort

explanation.surface: Manufacturing without hard work comes to a bloom of the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows, a river: the Indus runs through Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: A river is a 'flow-er'; the Indus flows through Pakistan in Asia.

clue.text: Nominally canine pirate

definitions.meaning: a traditional name for a pet dog
a sea robber

explanation.surface: A dog's name that belongs to a pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock name for a dog, and an old word for a sea robber or buccaneer.

clue.text: Selfishly saved, he'd set about road breaking

parts.note: the letters of he'd, apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: broken up, so the word's letters are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone who stashed things away is said to have attacked a road while breaking it up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking' turns ROAD into OARD; 'set about' puts HED round it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hoard is to stockpile greedily, so goods selfishly saved were stashed away.

clue.text: No points to either side in plea for universal affection

definitions.meaning: a tennis score of nil each
a call to cherish everyone

explanation.surface: With neither side scoring, someone calls for universal affection.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis, 'love' means zero, so the score where both players have nothing is called this.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennis calls a nil-nil score this, and read as words it urges cherishing everyone.

clue.text: Humanity matures and succeeds in coping

parts.note: man in the sense of mankind
ages means grows older, matures

explanation.surface: Humankind grows up and gets by.
explanation.definitionFit: To manage is to cope successfully with a task or situation.

clue.text: Steps taken when good people are about to go by bus

indicators.note: the saints stand around the other piece

parts.note: STS, saints, are good people
to ride is to travel as a passenger

explanation.surface: Long paces are taken when worthy folk are about to catch the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' looks like 'on the point of'; here 'about' means around, with 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Long paces are strides, so steps taken matches the plural noun.
